sentences.en: Being a celebrity can be boiled down to a simple formula.
sentences.zh: 成为名人可以归结为一个简单的公式。

sentences.en: Follow these rules and you can be an A-lister too.
sentences.zh: 遵循这些规则，你也能成为一线明星。

sentences.en: Rule number one, go to the right parties.
sentences.zh: 第一条规则：去对的派对。

sentences.en: It's the year's most electrifying red carpet.
sentences.zh: 这是年度最令人兴奋的红毯活动。

sentences.en: Rule number two, hang out with the right people.
sentences.zh: 第二条规则：和对的人混在一起。

sentences.en: One of the most successful singers in the biz, Selena Gomez and Taylor Swift.
sentences.zh: 业内最成功的歌手之一，赛琳娜·戈麦斯和泰勒·斯威夫特。

sentences.en: I mean, the two have been BFS for like ever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这两人简直是永远的好闺蜜。

sentences.en: Rule number three, be seen, but in small doses.
sentences.zh: 第三条规则：要露面，但要适度。

sentences.en: Overexposure, as we know, actually does make people lose intereSt.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，过度曝光确实会让人失去兴趣。

sentences.en: Rule number four, never go to Vegas.
sentences.zh: 第四条规则：永远别去拉斯维加斯。

sentences.en: What are you talking about, Vegas?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么，拉斯维加斯？
拉斯维加斯，宝贝，拉斯维加斯。

sentences.en: If you go to Las Vegas, it actually pulls your star power down.
sentences.zh: 如果你去拉斯维加斯，实际上会降低你的明星影响力。

sentences.en: Now maybe you're thinking, this episode isn't for me.
sentences.zh: 现在你可能在想，这集节目不适合我。

sentences.en: I have no desire to be one.
sentences.zh: 我也没有成为一线明星的欲望。

sentences.en: I don't read Us Weekly or Keep Up with the Kardashians.
sentences.zh: 我不看《美国周刊》，也不追《与卡戴珊姐妹同行》。

sentences.en: But Elizabeth Curd-Halkett's research into elite social groups might just apply to you too.
sentences.zh: 但伊丽莎白·柯里特-哈尔凯特对精英社交群体的研究可能也适用于你。

sentences.en: Elizabeth is a professor of urban planning at the University of Southern California.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白是南加州大学城市规划专业的教授。

sentences.en: But if you look at the books she's written, she's actually fascinated by social networks.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看她写的书，你会发现她其实对社交网络非常着迷。

sentences.en: From Hollywood to the highly educated people who spend their time and money on things like yoga, breastfeeding, buying organic food, attending farmers markets, listening to NPR,
sentences.zh: 从好莱坞到那些将时间和金钱花在瑜伽、母乳喂养、购买有机食品、逛农贸市场、收听NPR等事物上的高知群体，

sentences.en: reading the books on the New York Times bestseller liSt.
sentences.zh: 再到阅读《纽约时报》畅销书榜单上的书籍。

sentences.en: These are all physical manifestations of your cultural capital.
sentences.zh: 这些都是你文化资本的物理表现。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, elite groups and how our choices are shaped by the people around us.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》，探讨精英群体以及我们的选择是如何被周围的人所塑造的。

sentences.en: When you look at which stars shine the brightest in Hollywood, do you ever wonder why certain people are famous and not others?
sentences.zh: 当你观察好莱坞哪些明星最耀眼时，有没有想过为什么有些人出名而其他人不出名？

sentences.en: Talent certainly has something to do with it.

sentences.zh: 财富和美貌也很有帮助。

sentences.en: But in her book, Starstruck, Elizabeth says there's something else at work.
sentences.zh: 但在她的书《Starstruck》中，伊丽莎白说还有其他因素在起作用。

sentences.en: One thing that happens with, you know, interest fads and fashions and fixations on particular celebrities is that there is a collective intereSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，关于兴趣、潮流、时尚以及对特定名人的迷恋，发生的一件事就是存在一种集体兴趣。

sentences.en: But that collective interest is recursive.
sentences.zh: 但这种集体兴趣是递归的。

sentences.en: Meaning, if lots of people are paying attention to something or someone, that begets more attention.
sentences.zh: 意思是，如果很多人都在关注某事或某人，那就会引来更多的关注。

sentences.en: There are complicated reasons for why this is.
sentences.zh: 造成这种情况的原因很复杂。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I think really propels this kind of network effect is that in cultural markets and in taste,
sentences.zh: 我认为真正推动这种网络效应的原因之一是，在文化市场和品味方面，

sentences.en: which in many ways celebrities are a part of a taste-driven market, we look to each other for signals for what to pay attention to.
sentences.zh: （在很多方面，名人也是品味驱动市场的一部分），我们互相寻找信号来决定关注什么。

sentences.en: And in many ways, this explains the success of lots of taste-driven things.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这解释了许多品味驱动事物的成功。

sentences.en: So whether we're talking about films or music or artwork, are the objects or people who rise to the top really that much better or that much more interesting than everyone else?
sentences.zh: 所以，无论我们是在谈论电影、音乐还是艺术品，那些脱颖而出的人或物真的比其他人好得多或有趣得多吗？

sentences.en: The disproportionate win is a function of what economists call a winner-take-all market, which is that because we're looking for clues,
sentences.zh: 这种不成比例的胜出是经济学家所说的“赢家通吃”市场的功能，也就是说，因为我们在寻找线索，

sentences.en: we look at the person next to us and what they're paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 我们观察身边的人以及他们正在关注什么。

sentences.en: And so that then we pay attention to it, too, and then someone looks to us.
sentences.zh: 然后我们也去关注它，接着又有人观察我们。

sentences.en: And then it's really hard to say if that thing, whether it's a Mark Rothko painting or my friend on Facebook, is the thing to pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 所以真的很难说那个东西——无论是马克·罗斯科的画还是我在Facebook上的朋友——是否真的值得关注。

sentences.en: But by that point, we already are.
sentences.zh: 但到那时，我们已经在关注了。

sentences.en: When Elizabeth Currit-Halkett talks about celebrities, she isn't talking about all famous people.
sentences.zh: 当伊丽莎白·柯里特-哈尔凯特谈论名人时，她指的并不是所有出名的人。

sentences.en: She makes a distinction between people who are well-known and people who fascinate us.
sentences.zh: 她区分了“知名人士”和“让我们着迷的人”。

sentences.en: Fame is simply people knowing who you are.
sentences.zh: 名气仅仅是人们知道你是谁。

sentences.en: And the sheer number of people who know who someone is is very different from a public being fixated upon someone.
sentences.zh: 而知道某人是谁的人数，与公众对某人的痴迷程度是完全不同的。

sentences.en: Oh, that Bill Gates, isn't he in technology?
sentences.zh: 哦，那个比尔·盖茨，他不是搞科技的吗？

sentences.en: It's very different from what did Bill Gates eat for breakfast today and many, many people wanting to know.
sentences.zh: 这与“比尔·盖茨今天早餐吃了什么”以及许多许多人想知道这一点，是完全不同的。

sentences.en: It can be bewildering the way we care desperately about the details of some people's lives, but not others.
sentences.zh: 我们拼命关心某些人的生活细节，却不关心其他人，这种方式有时令人困惑。

sentences.en: Barack Obama is a popular politician, but not every president becomes a celebrity in the way that he did.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马是一位受欢迎的政治家，但并非每位总统都能像他那样成为名人。

sentences.en: I remember reading an article in the New York Times about the number of almonds Obama ate every night after dinner.
sentences.zh: 我记得读过《纽约时报》的一篇文章，讲的是奥巴马每晚饭后吃多少颗杏仁。

sentences.en: We know exactly which kind of socks Jennifer Aniston likes to wear and the type of diet Beyoncé followed after the birth of her first child.
sentences.zh: 我们确切地知道詹妮弗·安妮斯顿喜欢穿什么样的袜子，以及碧昂丝在生下第一个孩子后遵循什么样的饮食习惯。

sentences.en: I think that what has really changed, if we think about the evolution of celebrity, is that we have access to that material now.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果我们思考名人的演变，真正改变的是我们现在可以获取这些素材了。

sentences.en: So celebrities have existed in some shape or form since probably the beginning of human civilization.
sentences.zh: 所以，名人可能自人类文明之初就以某种形式存在了。

sentences.en: We've always been more interested in certain people for things that transcend their talent.
sentences.zh: 我们一直对某些人更感兴趣，原因往往超越了他们的才华。

sentences.en: And we've been more interested in the personal details of certain people.
sentences.zh: 而且我们一直对某些人的个人细节更感兴趣。

sentences.en: But in, you know, the Hollywood studio system, that was so much more controlled.
sentences.zh: 但在好莱坞制片厂制度下，那受到的控制要多得多。

sentences.en: And today it's not by virtue of many different things.
sentences.zh: 而今天，由于许多不同的原因，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: And so that focus on the number of almonds that President Obama used to eat, I want to say the number is seven.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于奥巴马总统过去常吃多少颗杏仁的关注——我想那个数字是七。

sentences.en: I'm not sure, but I remember that article and being very interested in this, that that is also a product of the fact that we can get that information.
sentences.zh: 我不确定，但我记得那篇文章，并且对此非常感兴趣，这也是因为我们能够获取这些信息。

sentences.en: Our ability to get that kind of personal information, coupled with the fact that we're drawn to what other people are drawn to, this is a formula for celebrity.
sentences.zh: 我们获取此类个人信息的能力，加上我们会被其他人所吸引的事物所吸引，这就是名人的公式。

sentences.en: We hear that Obama eats seven almonds and that other people care that Obama eats seven almonds.
sentences.zh: 我们听说奥巴马吃七颗杏仁，而且其他人也关心奥巴马吃七颗杏仁。

sentences.en: And suddenly this detail seems fascinating.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这个细节似乎变得引人入胜了。

sentences.en: It reminded me of a study that the researcher Stanley Milgrim once conducted in the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了研究员斯坦利·米尔格拉姆在20世纪60年代末进行的一项研究。

sentences.en: He had someone walk along a sidewalk in New York City.
sentences.zh: 他让一个人走在纽约市的人行道上。

sentences.en: The person walked down the street and then suddenly stopped and looked up.
sentences.zh: 那个人沿着街道走，然后突然停下来抬头看。

sentences.en: The experiment was documented in an educational video.
sentences.zh: 这项实验被记录在一部教育视频中。

sentences.en: We are all individuals, but we live in a world with other people and we must often accommodate to them.
sentences.zh: 我们都是个体，但我们生活在一个有其他人的世界里，我们必须经常迁就他们。

sentences.en: To what extent can we remain individuals in a social world?
sentences.zh: 在社交世界中，我们能在多大程度上保持个体性？

sentences.en: What kinds of pressures do others exert on us to conform?
sentences.zh: 他人会对我们施加什么样的压力来要求我们从众？

sentences.en: And how do we deal with such pressures?
sentences.zh: 我们如何应对这种压力？

sentences.en: How can social psychology study the issues of independence and conformity?
sentences.zh: 社会心理学如何研究独立与从众的问题？

sentences.en: Most pedestrians ignored the man and kept walking.
sentences.zh: 大多数行人无视那个人，继续走他们的路。

sentences.en: But a few passers-by, about 4%, stopped and they looked up too.
sentences.zh: 但有少数路人，大约4%，停下来也抬头看了看。

sentences.en: Then the experimenters had a larger group suddenly stop and look up.
sentences.zh: 然后实验者让一个更大的群体突然停下来抬头看。

sentences.en: When it wasn't just one person but a group, many more pedestrians stopped to look up as well.
sentences.zh: 当不仅仅是一个人而是一个群体时，更多的行人也停下来抬头看。

sentences.en: Nearly 20%, almost five times more than before.
sentences.zh: 接近20%，几乎是之前的五倍。

sentences.en: As they increased the size of the initial crowd, they found that the proportion of passers-by who imitated the looking-up response also increased.
sentences.zh: 随着他们增加初始人群的规模，他们发现模仿抬头反应的路人比例也随之增加。

sentences.en: We take our signals about what to pay attention to from one another.
sentences.zh: 我们从彼此那里获取关于关注什么的信号。

sentences.en: If one person's looking up, who cares?
sentences.zh: 如果只有一个人抬头看，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: But if 10 people are looking up, well, there must be something to see.
sentences.zh: 但如果有10个人抬头看，嗯，那一定有什么值得看的东西。

sentences.en: And there have been a number of different studies since Milgram where social scientists have looked at this as well.
sentences.zh: 自米尔格拉姆以来，还有许多不同的研究，社会科学家也对此进行了研究。

sentences.en: Anita Elberse did this really interesting study where she argued that big companies like Amazon actually create a collective,
sentences.zh: 安妮塔·埃尔伯斯做了一项非常有趣的研究，她认为像亚马逊这样的大公司实际上创造了一个集体，

sentences.en: cohesive fan base for things because they allow us to coalesce around big hits.
sentences.zh: 为事物创造了凝聚力的粉丝群，因为它们让我们围绕大热门聚集在一起。

sentences.en: There was another really interesting study done by Duncan Watts and Matthew Salganek where they did this fascinating study between two different groups of people listening to music.
sentences.zh: 邓肯·瓦茨和马修·萨尔加尼克做了另一项非常有趣的研究，他们在两组不同的人群中进行了一项关于听音乐的迷人研究。

sentences.en: Let's think about a popular song from a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 让我们想一想几年前的一首流行歌曲。

sentences.en: Now, the year that Call Me Maybe was released, 2012, there were a number of other pop songs that could have topped the charts.
sentences.zh: 现在，在《Call Me Maybe》发行的那一年，即2012年，还有许多其他流行歌曲本可以登上排行榜榜首。
比如，为什么不是这一首？

sentences.en: You could argue that Call Me Maybe was the catchiest song.
sentences.zh: 你可以说《Call Me Maybe》是最朗朗上口的歌曲。

sentences.en: But did you feel that way the first time you heard it?
sentences.zh: 但你第一次听到它时有这种感觉吗？

sentences.en: Or was it only after everyone else held up the song as the song of the summer?
sentences.zh: 还是说只有在其他人把它捧为“夏日之歌”之后？

sentences.en: That it started to get stuck in your head?
sentences.zh: 它才开始在你脑海中挥之不去？

sentences.en: When a song becomes popular, we get signals from lots of people that we should pay attention to it.
sentences.zh: 当一首歌变得流行时，我们会从很多人那里得到信号，告诉我们应该关注它。
我们一遍又一遍地听到它。

sentences.en: Then the hooks in our heads.
sentences.zh: 然后它就刻在了我们的脑海里。

sentences.en: And before we know it, we somehow know all the words.
sentences.zh: 在我们意识到之前，我们不知怎么地就记住了所有的歌词。

sentences.en: The takeaway was essentially that if you didn't know what other people were listening to,
sentences.zh: 结论本质上是，如果你不知道别人在听什么，

sentences.en: there was much more chaos in the list of the most popular music.
sentences.zh: 最流行音乐的榜单就会混乱得多。

sentences.en: It was much more ambiguous, you know, what everyone thought was the beSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大家认为什么是最好的，这会变得更加模糊。

sentences.en: But if listeners knew what others thought was good, that would actually compound upon itself.
sentences.zh: 但如果听众知道别人认为什么是好的，那实际上会产生叠加效应。

sentences.en: And then you got a much clearer list of the most popular songs.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会得到一份更清晰的最流行歌曲列表。

sentences.en: At the heart of your book is an argument about how celebrities become celebrities.
sentences.zh: 你书的核心是一个关于名人如何成为名人的论点。

sentences.en: And you say it has a lot to do with being part of a very elite, invite-only network.
sentences.zh: 你说这与成为一个非常精英、仅限受邀者的网络的一部分有很大关系。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
So when I started looking at celebrities, I was trying to figure out if there were particular personal attributes,
sentences.zh: 所以当我开始研究名人时，我试图弄清楚是否有特定的个人属性，

sentences.en: even talent attributes that drove, you know, the rise of a celebrity.
sentences.zh: 甚至是才华属性，推动了名人的崛起。

sentences.en: And it was really hard to come up with them.
sentences.zh: 要找出这些属性真的很难。

sentences.en: Simultaneously, I was really trying to understand the social dynamics of people who worked in creative industries.
sentences.zh: 同时，我真的试图理解在创意产业工作的人的社会动态。

sentences.en: My first book, The Whirl Hall Economy, was about how creative industries worked in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我的第一本书《The Whirl Hall Economy》是关于纽约创意产业如何运作的。

sentences.en: And it was a very qualitative book.
sentences.zh: 那是一本非常定性的书。

sentences.en: And I found when I spoke to artists and musicians and designers that despite the fact that they didn't have a lot of money
sentences.zh: 我发现当我与艺术家、音乐家和设计师交谈时，尽管他们没有很多钱，

sentences.en: and that a lot of them needed space to do their work, they felt compelled to live in New York City,
sentences.zh: 而且他们中的许多人需要空间来工作，但他们感到被迫住在纽约市，

sentences.en: even if, you know, getting a big warehouse space in Ohio would have served them well in a practical sense,
sentences.zh: 即使，你知道，在俄亥俄州获得一个大仓库空间在实际意义上对他们更有利，

sentences.en: that they needed their social lives in New York.
sentences.zh: 但他们需要纽约的社交生活。

sentences.en: And so when I finished that book, I really wanted to get a sense of the social networks
sentences.zh: 所以当我写完那本书时，我真的很想了解社交网络，

sentences.en: and the social milieu in which creative people, you know, lived and worked in and how important it was.
sentences.zh: 以及创意人士生活和工作的社会环境，以及它有多重要。

sentences.en: So I teamed up with my colleague, Gilad Ravid, and he and I looked at photographic data of celebrities.
sentences.zh: 所以我与我的同事吉拉德·拉维德合作，我和他查看了名人的摄影数据。

sentences.en: And we used Getty Images, and we looked at all of the caption information of photographs in their entertainment catalog
sentences.zh: 我们使用了盖蒂图片社，查看了他们娱乐目录中所有照片的说明信息，

sentences.en: over the course of one year.
And what we tried to do was make sense of not just who was in photographs together,
sentences.zh: 我们试图弄清楚的不仅是谁出现在同一张照片中，

sentences.en: but who went to the same parties, the same events, and where those parties were,
sentences.zh: 还有谁去了同一个派对、同一个活动，这些派对在哪里，

sentences.en: and if there was a pattern in who showed up at parties together.
sentences.zh: 以及谁一起出现在派对上是否有规律可循。

sentences.en: So was there a randomness to the photographs?
Was there something that drove why people showed up?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱动了人们出现的原因？

sentences.en: So what we tried to look at was a way to cut things off, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图寻找一种切入点，你知道，

sentences.en: so how could we organize all of these people in the database?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何组织数据库中的所有人？

sentences.en: So we looked at Forbes Star Currency, which ranked stars, you know, based on their star power,
sentences.zh: 所以我们查看了《福布斯》明星货币榜，它根据明星的影响力对明星进行排名，

sentences.en: and we divided them into the top 60 into three different groups, A-list, B-list, C-liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们将前60名分为三个不同的组：一线、二线、三线。

sentences.en: And we then looked at these stars in the photographs.
sentences.zh: 然后我们观察了照片中的这些明星。

sentences.en: So we corresponded these two different measures.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将这两种衡量标准对应起来。

sentences.en: And what we found was that the only group that had a non-random, very closed, connected network,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，唯一拥有非随机、非常封闭、紧密联系的网络，

sentences.en: a clique essentially, were the A-liSt.
sentences.zh: 本质上是一个小圈子的，就是一线明星。

sentences.en: And that they really reinforced their position by spending time with each other at the same parties over and over again
sentences.zh: 他们通过在同一个派对上反复相处来巩固自己的地位，

sentences.en: and not spending time with anyone else.
sentences.zh: 而不与其他任何人相处。

sentences.en: It was like a slumber party, you know.
sentences.zh: 就像睡衣派对一样，你知道。

sentences.en: It was amazing to be around so many wonderful women.
sentences.zh: 能和这么多出色的女性在一起真是太棒了。
那是一个一线明星睡衣派对。
